races.name: Racing TV Nursery Handicap
races.verdict: CROMANE was much improved upped to this trip when off the mark on her nursery debut at Naas a fortnight ago and looks capable of defying a 7 lb higher mark, perhaps at the expense of Scarlet Dream, who promises to be much better suited by this longer distance having been taken off her feet on her first foray into nursery company at Fairyhouse (6f) recently.

runners.note: Showed much improved form upped in trip when making a successful nursery debut in 13-runner event at Naas (1m, good to soft) 14 days ago. Has excellent follow-up claims.
Showed something like debut form in a refitted hood when third of 14 in maiden at Down Royal (7f, good) 27 days ago. Opening mark demands more but probably hasn't yet shown her all.

Showed a bit more than on debut when sixth of 9 in 1m maiden over C&D in July. Failed to repeat that effort at Gowran 9 weeks later but still showed signs of inexperience. Hood back on for handicap bow.
Has shown little in a trio of 6f maidens but is bred to fare better over this longer trip now handicapping.

races.name: EBF Slip Anchor Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: CAELUM shaped quite well on his Newcastle debut and might be able to improve past Lady Branksome, who sets the standard on her Ripon second but has been off since a disappointing effort at Chester in mid-June.

runners.note: 105,000 gns Minzaal half-brother to very smart 6f winner Powerful Glory. Showed speed when 4 lengths second on 5f Newcastle debut 4 weeks ago. Leading claims with improvement likely.
Ran her best race when third of 7 in maiden at Bath (5f, good to soft) 18 days ago but it's little better than modest form and leaves her with a bit to find here.

Much improved from her debut when second in 6f Ripon novice (good) in May. Possibly unsuited by soft ground when well held at Chester a fortnight later. Given a break since and sure to have a big say if back to the Ripon
66/1, eighth of 9 in novice at Beverley (5f, good) on debut 15 days ago. Needs to have come on a lot in a short time.
Fair form, best effort when third in a 5f Lingfield nursery (all-weather) in August. Respectable fifth in maiden at Southwell since.

races.name: Salisbury Annual Badgeholders 'Bluestocking' British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: Ralph Beckett has a fine record in this so his Frankel newcomer YAMANA, who fetched 1,500,000 guineas as a yearling, is taken to make a winning start at the chief expense of Somerton, who rates the clear pick of those with experience. A few other debutants also catch the eye though, including Gran Dia and the selection's stablemate Star Rose, in this fascinating novice.

runners.note: Foaled April 11. Without Parole gelding. Half-brother to 7f winner Slipper Time. Dam maiden (stayed 7f), half-sister to useful 6.7f-9f winner King's Slipper. The betting can guide for this newcomer.

Foaled April 8. 380,000 gns yearling, Lope De Vega colt. Half-brother to useful 2-y-o winner around 7f Composing. Dam, 1m-9.4f winner, half-sister to useful winner up to 7f Dolce Strega. Interesting debutant for leading

Kameko colt shaped encouragingly when a staying-on fourth of 8 in maiden at Newbury (6.5f, firm, 11/2) on debut 36 days ago. Can do better now up in trip.

Study of Man colt. Looked in need of the initial experience when sixth of 10 in novice at Ayr (1m, soft) 2 weeks ago. Open to improvement.

Ghaiyyath colt built on debut when third of 8 in novice at Goodwood (1m, soft) 32 days ago. Should improve further and holds good claims.
66/1, last of 7 in novice at Sandown (5f, soft) on debut 20 days ago. Significantly up in trip with plenty more required from this Saxon Warrior colt.
Foaled February 7. Mehmas filly. Closely related to high-class winner up to 1½m Pyledriver, and half-sister to several winners, including 1¼m-2m winner Shagpyle. Needs considering on her debut.

races.name: Bellewstown Inn Fillies Maiden
races.verdict: WHITE SAND BEACH needs to bounce back but sets the standard on her spring form and, freshened up by a short break, is worth one final chance to gain the win her pedigree demands. Tax Me Later improved from her course debut when a close second in a Gowran Park claimer and rates the main danger if progressing again for new connections, while Xirivella should be better suited by this shorter trip and

runners.note: Gregorian filly who looked one for the longer term when well held in 1m maiden at Navan on debut. Wears first-time tongue strap.

Placed on both starts to date but stepped up on debut when ½-length second of 8 to Quinta Girl in 1m claimer at Gowran earlier this month. Has since left Daniel McLoughlin and reverts to maiden company on first start for
Nando Parrado filly. Went with no promise when beating only a single rival in a 17-runner maiden at Fairyhouse 10 days ago.

Fairly useful filly who remains a maiden after 10 runs but has finished second on 4 occasions in this company. Failed to land the odds when only 3½ lengths fourth of 7 to Star Performer in 9f maiden at the Curragh last t
Ran to a fair level when placed in 1m maidens at Naas and Navan, but looked stretched by the step up to 9f at Punchestown last time. Back over shorter trip now but needs to improve.

races.name: Clonmel Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: This is wide open and it could pay to side with NELSON MUNTZ who returns from a break off a handy-looking mark and is taken to gain an overdue success at the chief expense of Downpatrick runner-up Dairy Force. Vaureal can also play a prominent role back in this sphere after a chasing victory at Punchestown. Max Meridius completes the shortlist back over a shorter trip.

runners.note: Scored over hurdle at Navan (2m) in November. Failed to get home when ninth of 15 in handicap chase at Downpatrick (29f, soft) when last seen 6 months ago. Not out of things back over hurdles reverted in trip.

Fair form in maiden hurdles at the end of 2025. Fit from the Flat (fair winner) and a potential improver in handicaps back hurdling. Worth a market check.
Seventeen runs since last win in 2024 but posted a good second of 10 in handicap hurdle at Downpatrick (2¼m, good to soft) 13 days ago, clear of the rest. Not taken lightly nudged up 2 lb.
Resumed winning ways in 12-runner handicap chase at Punchestown (2½m, good) in June. Reverts to hurdles and must enter calculations.
Won novice chase at Cork (17f) last season but failed to make much impact over hurdles all 3 starts this season for Gavin Cromwell. Needs this yard switch to spark a resurgence. Hood refitted.

Got off the mark in 2m maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan in June. Has run poorly switched to handicaps at Limerick and Kilbeggan (tongue tied) since, however.
Failed to see his races out in handicaps last season. Well held returning from 9 months off when seventh of 18 at Cork in August.
Still a maiden but in decent form until failing to stay when thirteenth of 16 in handicap hurdle at Navan (19f, good to soft) 12 days ago. May still do better back in trip in a first-time hood.
Free-going sort who gained a first success at Ballinrobe (17f) in July. Back on song with fifth of 15 in handicap hurdle there (2m, good) in August. Needs considering.
Is 0-7 and came in twelfth of 20 in handicap hurdle at Galway (17f, good to soft) 24 days ago. Others appeal much more.

races.name: Racedays For 9 Pound At Nottingham Racecourse Nursery
races.verdict: PRIDE OF TOLEDO is given a second chance to show that his mark is workable. Pure Mint had a possible excuse when turned over at short odds at Ascot last time and his debut success prior to that was highly promising so he's a potential big threat. Horndean and Washington Royale also make the shortlist.

runners.note: Won a 6f Salisbury novice in July. Acquitted himself well when fourth in a valuable sales race at York next time. Not in quite the same form when fifth of 15 on 6f Doncaster nursery since but the fact he went off favouri

Made the frame in a couple of maidens which have been working out well and duly took a step forward when second of 12 on 6f Lingfield nursery debut 3 weeks ago, pulling clear of the rest. Up 4 lb but still respected.

races.name: 'Pyledriver' British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 1)
races.verdict: The betting should prove highly informative here but Ed Walker's METICULOUSLY shaped with promise when a debut fourth at Leicester and this well-related son of Sioux Nation can build on it to thwart Ralph Beckett's New Bay newcomer Forest Bay, who appeals on pedigree. Gold Army has the form to play a prominent role, while Does Mary Know is not out of things if shrugging off a lesser effort at Asco

runners.note: Foaled April 11. 6,000 gns yearling, Ardad colt. Dam lightly-raced half-sister to useful 7f/1m winner Substantial out of smart 7f/1m winner Sentaril. Cheaply bought and the betting should reveal plenty.

Intello colt who has shaped with promise when twice placed over 7f in novice company at Kempton this summer, collared only late on when second of 10 on latter occasion. Holds solid form claims.

Foaled April 26. Time Test gelding. Brother to 1½m winner Kate The Cook. Dam, 1¼m-1¾m winner, is a half-sister to useful winner up to 1¼m Opera Baron. A considered newcomer, especially if the market vibes are positive.
Sent off 22/1 but made a promising debut amidst greenness when fourth of 9 in novice at Leicester (7f, good) 23 days ago. This well-related Sioux Nation colt seems sure to progress. Player.
Took a big step forward from his debut when fifth of 7 in novice at Haydock (6f, good to soft) 4 weeks ago. This son of Saxon Warrior is likely capable of better still.
50/1 for his debut but shaped encouragingly when sixth of 12 in 7f novice at Kempton in August. This Too Darn Hot colt looks open to improvement.

Foaled March 5. €75,000 foal, 70,000 gns yearling, Perfect Power colt. Half-brother to several winners, including 2-y-o 7f winner Tawafag and 5.3f/6f winner Fancy Dancer. Appeals on paper so this debutant needs a market

Mohaather colt hinted at promise when a debut seventh in maiden at Newbury in August but failed to build on it when eighth of 12 in similar company at Bath (1m, good to firm) 19 days ago.

Foaled April 15. 5,500 gns yearling, Harry Angel filly. Half-sister to 8.6f-1¼m winner Dashinwhitesargent and 7f winner Kennington. Dam, 7f/1m winner, is a half-sister to useful 2-y-o 6f winner Showout. No forlorn hope.

Foaled March 10. New Bay filly. Half-sister to numerous winners, including (at 1¼m) Forest Of Dean and Crown of Oaks and also 7f-1m scorer English Oak. Bred to be well above average for leading yard. Interesting debutant

races.name: Bluegrass Horse Feed Handicap (0-60)
races.verdict: GLASARMI looks potentially interesting down in grade. She's narrowly preferred to in-form Nephin Mountain and Glen Breeze, who makes only his second start over this trip.

Lightly-raced maiden from capable yard. Has little form in 5 starts to date, though.
Maiden who disputed favouritism when beaten 5½ lengths in this grade at Clonmel (1¼m) latest. Back down in trip on just fourth start current yard.

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap Chase
races.verdict: GONE IN SIXTY isn't an obvious follow-up candidate given his record but with Sean Bowen retaining the ride, he's worth chancing to defy a 5 lb higher mark for his Stratford success. Soldier In Mayo shaped well on last month's return/chasing debut behind a well-handicapped rival at Bangor and rates next best with improvement likely. Sedgefield scorer Socks Off rounds off the shortlist.

races.name: Slievenamon Claiming Hurdle
races.verdict: BLACK HEATHER hasn't been seen over hurdles for nearly 15 months but has been in solid form on the Flat this summer and is greatly favoured on these terms so gets the nod. C&D winner Rocky's Howya rates a major threat as he bids to extend his unbeaten sequence in claimers to 5, while Rich Belief and Allo Al Khawaneej also enter the reckoning.

races.name: Watch Racing TV Handicap
races.verdict: PACIFIC STORM has yet to show much but hails from a stable that has found form recently and can improve them markedly in handicaps so he's worth a chance to live up to the stamina in his pedigree in a race lacking depth. Corsican Caper and Noble Grace may be ones to pick up any pieces.

races.verdict: MOON ROCK was in need of the initial experience when a promising sixth in a valuable Ascot maiden and Ed Walker's Sea The Moon colt looks the way to go with improvement very much on the cards. Newcomers Showmaster and Vulcanist are in excellent hands and appeal on pedigree too so rate threats, especially if the market vibes are positive. Kamaal is another who can play a prominent role if rediscove

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap
races.verdict: LADY IN GOLD left her debut form well behind to score at Dundalk in February despite still looking a bit rough around the edges, so it's reasonable to assume she can progress further now entering handicap company. Tachos could well bounce back on her return to calmer waters, while Save The Sixes is another unexposed, well-bred filly who warrants respect.
